    1) intake (coordinator gathers plan + audience + success from bead)
    2) raw-failure-list (one overthinker member produces N failure reasons)
    3) deep-dive (N parallel members, one per failure reason; topology=turns within phase, freeform optional in v3)
    4) synthesis (coordinator/judge reads verdicts+findings, posts system.done with synthesized report)
- Coordinator runs in judge_mode: readonly. Cannot edit files.
- Each deep-diver is a thin wrapper over `overthinker` with the prospective-hindsight frame injected via task template.
- Output: HTML report + transcript written by a final write-capable specialist (executor with WRITE_LIMITED scope), or by Claude post-merge.

- Do not implement as a single specialist (specialists cannot spawn).
- Do not implement on v0/v1 mailbox — termination/synthesis needs the read-only judge from v2.
- No skill changes; the skill already documents the human-facing flow.

- Honors single-scheduler invariant: deep-diver wakeups go through node-supervisor.
- Per-member turn cap to prevent runaway deep-dives.
- Findings dual-write to node_memory until v3 derivation lands.

VALIDATION:
- `sp node run premortem.node.json --bead <test-bead>` produces report+transcript on a fixture plan.
- Coordinator terminates via system.done when all deep-divers post verdicts.
- No deep-diver edits files outside the report dir.

title: Add sp result --payload flag for complete startup-payload breakdown
description:
PROBLEM: There is no first-class command to inspect the complete startup
payload breakdown of a specialist run. The data exists as a
`payload_breakdown` timeline event (every component name, tokens, bytes,
plus totals), but reaching it requires the awkward incantation:
`sp feed <job-id> --json | jq 'select(.type=="payload_breakdown")'`.
`sp ps <id>` shows aggregate kb/tokens only. `sp db stats --with-payload`
shows totals per job, no component breakdown. `sp result <id>` shows the
last turn but not the startup payload.

SUCCESS: `sp result <id> --payload` (or equivalent flag like
`--show-payload` / `sp payload <id>`) prints the complete payload breakdown
in human-readable form by default, with `--json` for machine-readable.
Default human format shows:
  - one summary line: total_kb, total_tokens, n components
  - sorted-descending component table: name, tokens, bytes, percentage
  - source attribution if available (e.g. system_prompt vs bead_context vs
    own/parent/blocker)

Works on any job with a recorded payload_breakdown event (running, waiting,
done, error). Errors gracefully when the event is missing (e.g. very old
jobs from before the payload-instrumentation epic).

SCOPE: src/cli/result.ts (or new src/cli/payload.ts if the second flag
makes more sense). Reads the payload_breakdown event from
events.jsonl/timeline_events DB. Tests in tests/unit/cli/.

NON_GOALS:
- No change to the underlying payload_breakdown event schema.
- No new aggregation across multiple jobs (use sp db stats --with-payload).
- No live streaming — one-shot read of the most recent payload_breakdown
  event for the given job.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Match the existing `sp result --json` flag shape if extending sp result.
- Reuse formatPayloadBreakdownSummary / formatPayloadBreakdownTopComponents
  from src/cli/feed.ts where possible.
- Stale-job tolerance: jobs predating the payload epic should report
  "no payload breakdown recorded" rather than crash.

VALIDATION:
- Unit tests: happy path on a recent job, missing-event path on a synthetic
  old job, --json format stable.
- Manual smoke: `sp result <recent-job-id> --payload` against a few
  job-ids from this repo's observability.db.
- using-kpi skill SKILL.md updated with a recipe pointer to the new flag
  (replaces the awkward jq one-liner).

OUTPUT: Diff summary, manual smoke output examples, follow-up risks.

DISCOVERED-FROM: Asked during gzrx/release-pipeline session 2026-04-30.
Current workaround: sp feed <id> --json | jq 'select(.type=="payload_breakdown")'.

title: output_file: support dynamic path templates
description:
Currently output_file in the specialist schema is a static string path. This makes it useless for specialists that handle variable inputs (e.g. one video per run, one ticket per run) where the output filename should reflect the input.

CURRENT BEHAVIOR:
  output_file: 'transcripts/analysis.md'  # hardcoded, every run overwrites

DESIRED BEHAVIOR:
  output_file: 'transcripts/$video_id.analysis.md'  # resolved per-run from variables
  output_file: 'output/$bead_id.md'                 # resolved from bead context
  output_file: 'reports/$date-$specialist.md'      # resolved from runtime metadata

PROPOSED TEMPLATE VARIABLES (resolved at run time):
  $bead_id       — the bead ID passed via --bead
  $specialist    — the specialist name (metadata.name)
  $job_id        — the job ID of the current run
  $date          — ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD)
  $timestamp     — Unix timestamp
  Custom vars passed via --var key=value or extracted from bead notes

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE:
  runner.ts already extracts output_file at line 703. The render step
  could apply templateEngine.render() to the path string before
  writeFile(), using the same variables available to task_template.

DISCOVERED FROM:
  Building a YouTube transcriber specialist needing per-video output as
  transcripts/$video_id.analysis.md. Static output_file forces the
  specialist to do its own bash writes (fragile, stall-prone on large
  files).
notes: Deferred: useful feature, but not urgent in current pass.

title: Feature: sp ps renders bead dependency tree with job statuses
description:
sp ps currently shows a flat list of jobs. It should render the bead dependency tree (from bd dep) with jobs nested under their parent beads. This gives the operator a pipeline view at a glance.

Example output:
  unitAI-hfpo  Explore: sp ps vs sp feed divergence
    ✓ db218b  explorer  done  2m22s
    ├── unitAI-66xn  Fix: sp ps derives current_tool  P1
    │   ◉ 05cdf5  executor  running  3m34s  feature/unitAI-66xn-executor
    └── unitAI-yke7  Fix: clear current_tool in supervisor  P2
        ◐ 3b64a2  executor  waiting  2m00s  feature/unitAI-yke7-executor

Key design decisions:
- Beads are the tree nodes (from bd dep graph), jobs are leaves under their bead
- Dependencies drive nesting — parent beads at top, children indented
- Related beads (bd dep relate) shown as siblings
- Job status badges inline (✓ done, ◉ running, ◐ waiting, ✗ error)
- Maybe a --tree flag, or auto-detect when jobs share bead lineage
- Needs to query both bd (for bead deps) and job statuses (SQLite/status.json)

   - pi metadata: tools=yes, reasoning=yes

   - Source: probe with 'pi --print --model nvidia/nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning'
     against simple "use bash to echo TOOL_OK" prompt → response is a JSON

   - pi metadata: tools=no (correctly), reasoning=yes
   - Different failure: pi --print times out 60s+ because pi cannot parse
     NVIDIA NIM's separate `reasoning_content` delta-field in streaming.
     Direct API curl confirms model emits {"delta": {"reasoning": "...",
     "reasoning_content": "..."}} chunks BEFORE any "content" chunks; pi

      to handle non-OpenAI tool_calls patterns (DSML, <think>+JSON,
      reasoning_content streams). If pi has a translation hook, add one for
      these known patterns. If not, file an upstream issue with pi-coding-agent.

  (c) Document the safe-profile list of "tools=yes per pi metadata but actually
